To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
omega 3 longchain polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation has the potential to reduce the risk of developing retinal diseases of vascular and neural origin.

omega 3 longchain polyunsaturated fatty acid status is associated with retinal cell structure function and survival and that omega 3 fatty acids may have the potential to act in a cytoprotective role in retinal vascular and neural diseases.

omega 3 fatty acids have the capacity to modulate the expression and activity of bioactive compounds that are involved in the pathogenesis of vasoregulation, neovascularization and neurodegeneration in the retina.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of omega 6 and omega 3 LC PU FAs in the retina.
the role of omega 6 and omega 3 LC PUFA in health and disease in general, and in diseases of the retina, in particular.
the role of omega 6 and omega 3 LC PUFA in retinal physiology and pathophysiology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is evidence to suggest that LC omega 3 PUFAs are cytoprotective agents for the retina that may operate through a number of different mechanisms to prevent or attenuate the pathogenesis of retinal diseases.

omega 3 LCPUFAs are essential for the health and function of the retina and that omega 3 fatty acid deficiency is a risk factor for the development of a number of blinding retinal vascular and neurodegeneratve diseases.
omega 3 LCPUFAs may act to protect the retina from ischemic and inflammatory damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

omega 3 LCPFAs are essential for the maintenance of retinal function, and that tissue status of these compounds may modulate factors and pathways that are involved in the pathogenesis of blinding diseases of the retina.

LCPUFAS may act to: 1) attenuate the effects of ischemia and light induced oxidative stress, 2) inhibit the production of inflammatory eicosanoids and pro inflammatory cytokines, 3) inhibit the expression of VEGF receptors and VEGF induced angiogenesis, 4) modulate expression of matrix metalloproteinase and interstitial collagenase, 5) attenuate the expression of NFkappaB and COX 2, 6)

omega 3 fatty acids have the capacity to modulate retinal structure and functions that are affected by environmental factors and disease processes that contribute to the development of vasoproliferaive and neurodegeneratve retinal diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are a number of plausible mechanisms to support the notion that dietary omega 3 fatty acids have the capacity to protect and restore the health of the retina.
there are many potential targets of omega 3 LCUPFAs in the retina.
omega 3 dietary LCPUFA status may influence the course of retinal disease.
